description: Shared Renovate preset for kachkaev’s repos, consumed as `github>kachkaev/reusable-stuff:renovate-preset`. The top-level `minimumReleaseAge` is the floor that keeps Renovate from proposing a version pnpm would refuse to lock, so it must stay in sync with the same option in each repo’s pnpm-workspace.yaml. Rules below may raise it, never lower it.

customManagers.description: TODO: delete this manager once renovatebot/renovate#38067 is closed and Renovate reads `devEngines` natively. Until then this JSONata manager extracts the Node.js runtime version from package.json. It handles `devEngines.runtime` as either a single object or an array and only picks entries named `node`. Renovate rewrites the value by searching for it in the file, then re-runs this query to confirm the right field changed.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh lock files on Monday mornings without waiting for dashboard approval. The top-level `:dependencyDashboardApproval` would otherwise park this under “Pending Approval” every week; `:maintainLockFilesWeekly` is not used because it only enables the job and takes the default schedule. `minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour` is overridden because a lock file maintenance branch carries one synthetic upgrade per package file with no `releaseTimestamp` — Renovate delegates the resolution to the package manager and never looks up individual releases. Under the default `timestamp-required`, the inherited top-level `minimumReleaseAge` therefore makes `renovate/stability-days` pending forever, so the weekly PR can never be merged. `timestamp-optional` lets a timestamp-less upgrade count as stable; the 8 hour floor is still enforced here, because pnpm applies its own `minimumReleaseAge` from pnpm-workspace.yaml while regenerating the lock file.

packageRules.description: The top-level `pin` range strategy applies to every dependency type, including ones that are ranges by design: `engines` describes which runtimes a package supports rather than a version to install, `peerDependencies` describes compatibility, and the `node-version` input of `actions/setup-node` names a release line. Pinning those produces PRs like `>=22.15.0` → `v26.8.1` and `22` → `22.23.2`, which narrow guarantees instead of updating anything. Restoring `auto` for them leaves in-range releases alone and only proposes out-of-range updates.

TODO: once renovatebot/renovate#38067 is closed and the manager above is deleted, re-check `matchDatasources` and `matchDepTypes` here against what the built-in npm manager reports for `devEngines`. Node.js runtime updates found by that manager. Minor and patch releases are automerged on the same weekend cadence as devDependencies. Majors wait for dashboard approval: the dev runtime is what tests run on, and keeping it on the oldest supported line is what backs the `engines` claim.

`engines` declares which runtimes a package supports, so any change there is a compatibility decision and a breaking one when the floor rises. Every such update waits for dashboard approval and never automerges, whatever the update type. This overrides the patch rule above.

The `node-version` input of `actions/setup-node` names the release line a workflow, or a published composite action, runs on. Major bumps there change the runtime for everything that uses it, so they wait for dashboard approval instead of automerging with the other GitHub Actions updates.
